evidence.original_text: The Academy of Military Science (AMS) was a six-week officer commissioning program of the United States Air Force. AMS was held at Maxwell Air Force Base in Montgomery, Alabama, with the purpose of training and commissioning Air National Guard officers only.[1] AMS was originally located at McGhee Tyson Air National Guard Base, outside Knoxville, Tennessee. It was moved to Maxwell in 2009.

AMS is run by Air National Guard Detachment 12 for administrative purposes, but daily operation of AMS falls under the operational control of OTS. Det. 12 is a "total force" (staffed by all three Air Force components) organization with 25 positions within the academy's system, plus a position assigned to the Air University's Holm Center and another assigned as deputy commander of the Det. 12. AMS has been a total force organization since 1994.[2]

The memorandum of agreement the Holm Center commander and the Air National Guard Readiness Center commander was finalized May 26, 2009. That agreement specified how AMS would operate at Maxwell. The first AMS class at Maxwell began in October 2009. Each class includes approximately 125 students.
In March 2014, AMS switched to an eight-week course until it was shut down in January 2015, and fully integrated into Air Force OTS.

value.text:
The Academy of Military Science (AMS) was an officer commissioning program of the United States Air Force for Air National Guard officers. It was held at Maxwell Air Force Base in Montgomery, Alabama, after moving from McGhee Tyson Air National Guard Base near Knoxville, Tennessee, in 2009. Its curriculum resembled that of Air Force Officer Training School, but its course was initially six weeks long. The program did not use the upper-class and lower-class structure described for Officer Training School.

AMS was administered by Air National Guard Detachment 12, while its daily operations fell under Officer Training School operational control. An agreement governing its operation at Maxwell was finalized on May 26, 2009, and the first class there began in October of that year. The account describes each class as including approximately 125 students. In March 2014, the course expanded to eight weeks. It shut down in January 2015 and was fully integrated into Air Force Officer Training School.
